# Use Le Chat to Turn a Long Recipe into a Simple Shopping List

> **In short:** Paste a recipe with roughly twelve ingredients into Le Chat, ask it to build a grouped shopping list, and copy the result to your phone before you head to the store. It usually takes under two minutes, and you don't need a paid plan.

You're standing in the kitchen holding your phone, scrolling past a recipe with ingredients scattered across two paragraphs of backstory. You want a clean shopping list — now, not in twenty minutes. Le Chat, the chat assistant from the French AI company Mistral, can turn that wall of text into a tidy, grouped list you can tick off aisle by aisle. This guide shows you exactly how to set that up, even if you've never opened an AI assistant before.

## Before you start

- **A free Le Chat account.** Sign up at `chat.mistral.ai` with an email or a Google account. The free plan covers this task fully — you don't need to pay.
- **A recipe.** Pick any recipe with around a dozen ingredients. A long one from a food blog or a cookbook page works best, because the messier the original, the more obvious the time savings.
- **About five minutes.** Two minutes to paste and ask, two or three to tweak the list, and maybe a minute to copy it to your notes app.
- **A phone or computer.** Le Chat works on both. If you're heading to the store right after, use your phone so you can copy the list straight into Notes, Google Keep, or any list app you already use.

A small honest note before we start: Le Chat can organize and reword the ingredients for you, but it can't check your pantry or merge two recipes into one. If you want to combine three recipes into a single list, you'll need to paste them together as one message — see Step 4 for that variation.

## Step 1 — Open Le Chat and start a new chat

Go to `chat.mistral.ai` in your browser, or open the Le Chat app if you already installed it. On the home screen, look for a **button labeled "New chat"** — usually at the top-left of the screen, sometimes shown as a square plus icon in the corner of the sidebar. Click or tap it once.

You'll see a fresh, empty chat window with a text box near the bottom and a paperclip or attachment icon next to it. The blank box is where you'll paste the recipe. If you can't see a "New chat" button, look for a pencil icon or a chat-bubble with a plus sign — apps shift these around between updates.

💬 Example: if you're on the home screen and unsure, type anything short like "hi" first to confirm the chat box is responsive.

You'll know it worked when the page shows an empty conversation with no previous messages, and the text box cursor blinks at the bottom — ready for you to paste in.

## Step 2 — Paste the full recipe into the chat box

Open your recipe on the same screen or in another tab, highlight every line of ingredients (including the measurements — "2 cups flour", "1 tbsp olive oil", "a pinch of salt"), and copy it. Then click into Le Chat's empty text box and paste. On a phone, long-press inside the box and tap **Paste**.

You'll see the recipe appear as a block of text inside your message bubble — usually in plain monospace style. The whole ingredient section should fit, even if it's long, because Le Chat handles long messages well. If your recipe includes images of the dish, don't paste those — just the text of the ingredients.

If it looks different: on the phone app the text box might sit behind the keyboard at first. Tap inside it once so the keyboard rises, then paste. On desktop, the standard `Ctrl+V` (Windows) or `Cmd+V` (Mac) works as expected.

You'll know it worked when the recipe text sits in your message bubble, still highlighted or unhighlighted but visible, and the send arrow (→) or paper-plane icon lights up in the corner of the box.

## Step 3 — Ask Le Chat to build a grouped shopping list

Now write a short instruction under the pasted recipe (or as a new message right after it — both work). Tell Le Chat exactly what shape of list you want: grouped by store section, no extra commentary, and copy-paste friendly. Be specific — the more concrete your ask, the cleaner the output.

You'll see a "Thinking…" or pulsing dots indicator for a few seconds, and then Le Chat replies with a formatted list. It usually uses headings like **Produce**, **Dairy**, **Pantry**, and bullet points under each — but the exact groups depend on the ingredients, so don't be surprised if "Spices" or "Frozen" shows up for one recipe and not another.

💬 Example prompt you can copy and adapt:

> "Group these ingredients into a shopping list by store section (produce, dairy, meat, pantry, spices, frozen). Show quantities. Give me just the list — no intro paragraph, no tips, no closing line. Use simple bullet points I can copy into my notes app."

You'll know it worked when the response is mostly bullet points and headings, with no extra explanation paragraphs around them. If you see a friendly sentence like "Here's your list!" before the list, that's fine — just delete it when you copy.

## Step 4 — Tweak the list or combine recipes

This is the optional moment to adjust. Look through the list and check two things: are the quantities right, and do any items overlap? If you're combining two recipes, paste the second one below the first in the same message (or as a follow-up) and ask Le Chat to merge them into one list with quantities added together.

On screen, Le Chat rewrites the list with the merged quantities — for example, three recipes each calling for "1 onion" become "3 onions" on one line. If a recipe says "a handful of cilantro" and another says "2 tbsp chopped cilantro", Le Chat usually picks one and notes the difference. Read it over — this is the moment to fix anything that looks off.

If it looks different: if Le Chat's reply is in a long paragraph instead of bullets, your prompt wasn't specific enough. Send a follow-up like "Reformat as bullet points only, no sentences." It will redo it.

You'll know it worked when you can read the whole list in under thirty seconds, every quantity is a number you trust, and nothing important is missing. If something's wrong — wrong unit, wrong amount, missing item — type the fix as a quick follow-up: "Change 200g butter to 1 stick" or "Add 1 lime to produce."

## Step 5 — Copy the list to your phone and head out

Highlight Le Chat's reply (or just tap **Copy** if your browser offers a copy button on the code-style blocks), then open your notes app — Apple Notes, Google Keep, Samsung Notes, or even a plain text message to yourself. Paste it in.

You'll see the headings and bullets come across cleanly in most modern notes apps. Some apps flatten the bullets into plain lines, but the structure (Produce / Dairy / etc.) usually survives as section titles. Pin the note to the top of your list so it's the first thing you see in the store.

If it looks different: in Safari on iPhone, you may need to use **Share → Select All → Copy** instead of dragging to highlight, because long AI replies can be tricky to grab. In the Le Chat mobile app, look for a small **copy icon** at the top-right of each AI message — tap it once and the whole reply goes to your clipboard.

You'll know it worked when the list is on your phone, readable at a glance, with store sections as headers and quantities next to each item. Walk into the store, tick items as you drop them in the cart, and toss the note when you get home.

## Common mistakes

- **Asking without a format.** "Make me a shopping list" usually gives a paragraph of ingredients. Always say *grouped by section, bullet points only, no intro or outro* — otherwise you'll spend more time editing than you saved.
- **Forgetting the quantities.** Le Chat can summarize measurements ("a pinch", "to taste") or drop them entirely. If you care about exact amounts, add to your prompt: *"Keep the quantities — don't drop '1 tbsp' or '200 g'."*
- **Trusting the list blindly.** AI assistants occasionally misread a measurement (1 tbsp can become 1 tsp). Spend ten seconds scanning the list before you leave — it's faster than walking back to the store for a missing ingredient.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** the next time a friend sends you a link to "the best lasagna ever," you can have a printed-and-ready shopping list in two minutes flat. It also works for meal prep — paste four dinner recipes at once and Le Chat merges them into one master list for the week.
- **For your work or business:** if you run a small café, catering side-business, or a cooking class, this same trick turns any recipe PDF into a clean prep list for your team. The "no intro, no closing, bullet points only" format becomes a reusable prompt you keep in a note.
- **If you're just getting started:** don't worry about prompt engineering. One sentence — *"Group by store section, keep quantities, bullet points only"* — is enough to get a usable list nine times out of ten. Iterate from there.

## Try it now

Pick a recipe you've been meaning to cook. Open `chat.mistral.ai`, paste the ingredients, and send this exact prompt:

> "Group these ingredients into a shopping list by store section. Keep quantities. Bullets only, no intro or closing."

Copy whatever Le Chat gives you into your notes app. That's the whole flow — and from now on, every recipe you save is two minutes away from the store.
